newsitem.title: UK: Russia raises $2.0 billion with 10-year bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Russia raises $2.0 billion with 10-year bond issue.

text.p: Russia on Thursday raised $2.0 billion, twice the amount originally expected, in the international capital markets with the launch of a 10-year Eurobond.
The deal, modern Russia's third since its market debut last November, ranks among the largest Eurobonds ever and dealers reported huge demand for paper after a series of roadshows around the world.

The bond was launched with a 10.00 percent coupon, a key psychological level. Double-digit coupons are something of a rarity in the current low interest rate environment and are particularly attractive to retail investors.
Final pricing at a yield spread of 375 basis points over U.S. Treasuries was due later, after the New York opening. J.P. Morgan Securities and SBC Warburg were joint lead managers.
Russia first tapped the international capital markets in November 1996 with a $1.0 billion five-year bond.
In March, it raised 2.0 billion marks ($1.2 billion) via a seven-year bond. Today's deal brought the 1997 total to around $3.2 billion.
Last Friday, Russian deputy finance minister Mikhail Kasyanov told a news conference it would borrow up to $3.5 billion from international bond markets this year.
That figure was based on Russia also launching a global dollar bond in the autumn.
On the basis of Russia's deals so far, such a global bond would have to be for a minimum $500 million and more likely $1.0 billion, dealers said, thus busting Russia's recent forecast.
Kasyanov also said Russia would raise $3.0-3.5 billion internationally in 1998. "That is an appropriate amount for us using this source of funding," he said.
